title: Serial Divisible-by-5 (3 Flip-Flops)
constraints: Bits of an arbitrarily long binary number arrive **MSB first**, one per rising edge with `valid`. After each edge, `d5 = 1` when the number received so far is divisible by 5 (combinational from the state). Synchronous reset starts a new number (the empty number is 0, so `d5 = 1`).
At most **3 flip-flops**: you can't store the number.
hints: Appending a bit b to a number n gives 2n + b. Only n mod 5 matters for the next remainder.
Keep r = n mod 5 (5 states → 3 flops): `r <= (2r + b) mod 5`, as a 5 × 2 table.

examples.title: long
examples.expected: d5 tracks the running value mod 5
